_AI_AGENT_INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Goal: build <submission_folder>/judges.json describing the hackathon's real judging panel (or a realistic stand-in panel) so each judge can be simulated in its own isolated E2B MicroVM.
2. The panel may contain ANY number of judges from 1 to 10 (1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8...). Add or delete judge blocks; each top-level key that does not start with '_' is one judge id.
3. Judge ids: short ASCII snake_case such as 'J1_local_web3_reviewer' (letters, digits, '_' and '-' only; anything else is replaced by '_'). Prefer role-based ids over real names.

4. tier: 'TIER_1_LOCAL' (fast generalist triage, sees a 350-word excerpt + non-SME evidence), 'TIER_2_SME' (technical expert, sees the full text + all evidence) or 'TIER_3_EXEC' (sponsor / executive, sees the 350-word excerpt + all evidence). Aliases are normalized automatically: 'LOCAL' -> TIER_1_LOCAL, 'SME' / 'TECHNICAL' / 'EXPERT' -> TIER_2_SME, 'EXEC' / 'VIP' / 'SPONSOR' -> TIER_3_EXEC. Unknown values become TIER_2_SME.

5. preferred_model: Gemini model id for this judge (empty string = the --model CLI default). temperature: 0.0-2.0 (0.45-0.70 recommended; vary it across judges for diversity). time_limit_sec: the simulated review budget per project (180-300 is realistic).
6. queue_pressure: one sentence placing the project in the judge's queue, e.g. 'Project 12 of 60 in the DeFi track queue (simulated 240-second review budget)'.

7. role: fill the guided fields from the judge's PUBLIC professional footprint (official judge page, LinkedIn summary, GitHub, talks, papers, blog posts). title = one line persona; bio = 2-4 sentences; expertise = list; signature_criteria = what this judge rewards most; red_flags = what makes this judge lower a score; judging_style = how they inspect a project.

8. Use ONLY public, professional information. Never include private data (personal contact details, family, health, home address, private social media). Never write content that mocks or misrepresents a real person; describe the judging lens, not the individual.
9. 'role' may also be a single plain-text paragraph instead of the guided object.
10. Validate the result is strict JSON before saving. Keys starting with '_' (like this block) are ignored by the tool.

J1_local_generalist_reviewer.queue_pressure: Project 34 of 42 in the local triage queue (simulated 180-second / 3-minute review budget)

role.title: a local hackathon judge and product-minded generalist reviewing dozens of projects in one session
role.bio: <2-4 sentence public professional bio: current role, organization type, years of experience, communities served>
signature_criteria: <what this judge rewards most, e.g. a demo that works in the first 30 seconds>
red_flags: <what lowers the score, e.g. a broken live URL>
role.judging_style: <e.g. opens the live demo first, skims the README second, ignores long text>

J2_technical_sme_reviewer.queue_pressure: Finalist 9 of 30 in the technical expert review batch (simulated 300-second / 5-minute review budget)

role.title: a subject-matter expert judge who inspects the code, the architecture and the evidence
role.bio: <2-4 sentence public professional bio: engineering / research background, notable public projects or papers>
signature_criteria: <e.g. passing tests on a clean clone>
red_flags: <e.g. thin wrapper around an API presented as novel research>
role.judging_style: <e.g. clones the repo, reads the tests, checks every cited dataset URL>

J3_sponsor_exec_reviewer.queue_pressure: Finalist 5 of 12 on the sponsor / executive final ballot (simulated 240-second executive briefing window)

role.title: an executive or sponsor judge deciding which finalists receive the official prizes
role.bio: <2-4 sentence public professional bio: leadership role, organization mission, public statements about what they look for>
signature_criteria: <e.g. meaningful use of the sponsor's technology>
role.judging_style: <e.g. reads the first slide and the pitch, then asks which prize the project truly deserves>
